posts.title: Promoting Safer Anesthesia Practice: SACRA's First Student Research Initiative
posts.summary: An overview of SACRA's inaugural student research effort focused on anesthesia safety checklists and monitoring protocols at Kibogora Polytechnic.
posts.author: Olivier Twubahimana
posts.content: Anesthesia safety remains a critical priority in Rwanda's growing healthcare system. In our first year of operation, SACRA members at Kibogora Polytechnic undertook a structured review of pre-induction safety checklist compliance in local clinical settings. Students observed and documented checklist adherence in collaboration with clinical supervisors during practical training rotations. The study highlighted areas where standardized checklists significantly improved procedural safety awareness among students. This research initiative marks a turning point for student-led evidence-based practice at Kibogora Polytechnic and demonstrates the value of embedding research culture from the earliest years of anesthesia training.

posts.title: Welcome Our 2026–2027 Executive Board Members
posts.summary: Announcing the newly elected student leaders heading SACRA's research committees and community health campaigns at Kibogora Polytechnic.
posts.author: Jean-Claude Niyonisaba
posts.content: We are thrilled to officially announce the results of the 2026 SACRA Leadership Elections at Kibogora Polytechnic, Rusizi Campus. Students voted to elect members across all executive committee positions. Our new board is dedicated to deepening community health outreach, strengthening peer-mentorship programs, and expanding SACRA's research and training activities. The incoming team brings fresh energy and commitment to SACRA's mission of public health awareness and student empowerment. Read on to learn more about the new President, Vice President, and committee chairs for this academic year.

posts.title: Hands-On Simulation Training: Building Skills in Kibogora Polytechnic's Clinical Lab
posts.summary: A look at how simulation-based training at Kibogora Polytechnic is enhancing anesthesia crisis management skills among students.
posts.author: Eric Ndahimana
posts.content: Simulation training is a cornerstone of anesthesia education, and Kibogora Polytechnic's clinical skills lab offers students a structured environment to practice crisis resource management. SACRA organized hands-on simulation sessions where students worked through perioperative emergency scenarios using available mannequins and monitoring equipment. These drills reinforced team communication, drug dosage decision-making, and airway management principles. The sessions complemented classroom learning and gave students supervised exposure to real-world emergency protocols before entering clinical rotations. SACRA plans to expand these monthly simulation sessions to all year groups in the upcoming semester.

posts.title: Outreach Highlight: Anesthesia Awareness in Rural Clinics
posts.summary: A review of our student campaigns in regional health centers, promoting airway checklists and monitoring protocols across Rusizi District.
posts.author: Divine Mutesi
posts.content: Patient safety in remote clinics is highly dependent on standardized checklists and trained personnel. Last month, SACRA members visited local primary care clinics in the Rusizi District. We introduced the WHO Safe Surgery Checklist and organized interactive demonstrations with clinic staff. Students facilitated short training sessions to help health workers understand the importance of pre-procedure verification, oxygen monitoring, and emergency protocols. In this post, we review what we observed during the visits and outline SACRA's upcoming outreach schedule for the second half of 2026.
